repo.description:
SurrealDB fetches the JWKS document for a JWT or record access method over the network, gated by `--allow-net`/`--deny-net`. The check in `core/src/iam/jwks.rs` (`check_capabilities_url`) validates only the URL **host string**; the fetch then runs on a `reqwest` client using the default DNS resolver, with no check on the resolved addresses. An Owner can point an access method at an `--allow-net`-permitted hostname that resolves to loopback, link-local, cloud-metadata, or private address space, causing the server to issue a GET to that internal address - one a direct URL to the same IP would block.

### Impact

What an attacker **can** do:

- With the **Owner** role at database level or above (the minimum to run `DEFINE ACCESS ... TYPE JWT URL` / `TYPE RECORD ... WITH JWT URL`), point an access method at an allow-listed hostname resolving to an internal address, causing a GET the allowlist was meant to block (loopback, `169.254.169.254`, RFC 1918).
- Infer internal host/port liveness from response-timing and JWKS-parse-success differences.

What it **can't** do:

- Read the response - the fetch is blind (body parsed only as a JWKS; failures surface as an opaque `InvalidAuth` error).
- Modify data or affect availability (a single GET).

### Patches

The JWKS fetcher now uses the same capability-aware DNS resolver as the protected `HttpClient`, re-checking every resolved address and blocking private/special-use IPs unless explicitly allow-listed.

- Versions 3.2.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### Workarounds

- Use only trusted JWKS hosts that resolve to fixed public addresses, or use locally defined keys instead of a remote JWKS.
- Restrict the Owner role to trusted operators.
- Enforce network-layer egress filtering (block loopback, `169.254.0.0/16`, and internal ranges).

### References

- [SurrealDB Documentation - Capabilities](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealdb/security/capabilities)
- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE ACCESS](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/access)
- `fix(core): enforce JWKS network capabilities at the resolved IP` (included in SurrealDB 3.2.0)

### Acknowledgements

Thanks to [@DavidCarliez](https://github.com/DavidCarliez) for finding and reporting this issue.
repo.summary: SSRF via JWKS URL - allow-listed hostname resolving to a private IP
